e: A boat capsizes near Isla de Mona following a fight involving a machete. The United States Coast Guard rescues at least 40 people. Three people are killed.
A magnitude 4.8 earthquake hits Yauco, injuring three people.
The Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority begins temporarily shutting off water in the San Juan area due to water shortages.
Governor Gonzalez announces the resignation of her Chief of Staff, Francisco Domenech, and his deputy, Itza García, amid allegations of irregularities at the Puerto Rico Office of Permit Management.
Governor Gonzalez declares a state of emergency in response to increased coastal erosion in the northern part of the island.
Sebastián Negrón Reichard resigns as Secretary of Economic Development and Commerce of Puerto Rico, citing excessive interference by the Gonzalez administration.

A protest over a rate fare increase results in the Puerto Rican government temporarily shutting down ferry service between the main island and Vieques. The protest is held in response to an increase in price from $2 to $11.25 for those who do not live on Vieques.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents are deployed to 14 airports nationwide, including Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport.
Police seize $12 million worth of cocaine found on a drug smuggling boat off the island's northern coast. Three suspects are arrested.
A patient is killed in a gun attack on an ambulance in Santurce.
Governor Gonzalez signs a law recognizing a fetus as a human being.
The Public Housing Administration orders a compulsory inspection of 56,000 units at 328 projects across the territory following criticism over subhuman living conditions.
